html:
SMTO-TSK-0041 — This conversation already has 32 tasks waiting

GUID: 00bc6ea2-01d6-402d-8617-9c4d435a0e32
Slug: task-queue-limit
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • A conversation can hold up to 32 waiting tasks, and this one is full, so your new message wasn't added. The tasks already waiting are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Queued list in this conversation and look through the waiting tasks. Seeing what is waiting helps you decide what can go.
  2. Delete any waiting task you no longer need with its trash button (Delete queued task). Each task you remove frees a place for your new one.
  3. Or wait until the current task finishes and the next one starts, then send your message. A place opens each time a waiting task starts running.

What success looks like

  • Your message appears in the Queued list.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use Clear queue unless you really want to remove every waiting task; it deletes all of them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Enqueue was rejected because the conversation lane already holds the maximum of 32 future (unstarted) queued tasks.

What this means

  • Enqueue counts 32 existing future queued tasks in the conversation lane and rejects another. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Enqueue counts 32 existing future queued tasks in the conversation lane and rejects another.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the current future queue, distinguishing unstarted items from active work and accepted submissions.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the lane's queued_tasks (unstarted items only; the active task does not count). Let queued work advance, or delete specific unstarted tasks through the lane's delete control, before enqueueing again; do not split or duplicate submissions to get around the 32-task limit.
  • Wait for queued work to progress or deliberately remove an unstarted future task before adding another. Do not create duplicate tasks to bypass the queue bound.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Normal queue progress or deliberate removal of an unstarted item releases a slot.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
